AgentCostStats.description: Statistics for a specific agent alias.

cached_input_tokens.description:
Cached input tokens (subset of `input_tokens` served from the
provider's prompt cache).

cost_usd.description: Total cost attributed to this agent for the period.

input_tokens.description:
Input tokens (uncached + cached). Matches each record's
`input_tokens` field.

request_count.description: Number of LLM responses attributed to this agent for the period.

total_tokens.description: Total tokens attributed to this agent for the period (input + output).

name.description:
Agent alias — also the key written to `agents.<name>`. Must
not collide with an existing agent alias; runtime validation
rejects collisions before apply.

personality_file.description:
Optional personality file path written to
`agents.<name>.personality_file`. `None` ships the agent with
no personality file (the existing optional pattern).

personality_files.description:
Staged personality file contents to write into the agent's
workspace during the atomic apply. Empty list = no files
written. Surfaces validate the filename against the canonical
`EDITABLE_PERSONALITY_FILES` list before staging.

system_prompt.description:
System prompt text. Sourced from the personality template
picker in the UI (`default` or `blank`); Quickstart does not
pre-fill this field itself.

ApprovalDecision.description: Approve or deny a waiting SOP gate.

oneOf.description:
Approve a deterministic checkpoint WITH an operator amendment: `text`
replaces the step's declared editable field (`- edit:` bullet) in the
piped value before the run resumes. Checkpoint-only; an approval gate
(broker-owned `WaitingApproval`) refuses it fail-closed.

Ask for a re-draft: re-run the checkpoint's predecessor `llm.generate`
step with `guidance` framed as reviewer feedback, then re-present the
gate (revision + 1). Checkpoint-only, same as `Amend`.

BoundTriggerSource.description: A non-channel trigger source and the fields needed to configure it.

BuilderSubmission.description: Complete builder submission consumed by the shared Quickstart apply path.

agent.description: Agent identity (always create-new — there's no reuse path).

channels.description:
Channels step. 0..N entries. Each is either a freshly-built
[`ChannelQuickStart`] or the alias of an existing channel.
The agent's `channels` field is auto-bound to every entry in
this vec at apply time.

memory.description:
Memory step. Either a fresh [`MemoryChoice`] or the alias of
an existing `storage.<type>.<alias>` entry.

model_provider.description:
Model provider step submission. Always a `Create new` shape
in this initial cut — `Use existing` is represented by
[`SelectorChoice::Existing`] in the wrapper enum below.

peer_groups.description:
Peer groups to materialize. Each entry can reference either a
staged channel from `channels` (above) or an already-configured
channel ref. Empty list = no peer-group rows written.

risk_profile.description:
Risk profile preset key from [`RISK_PRESETS`], or the alias
of an existing `risk-profiles.<alias>`.

runtime_profile.description:
Runtime profile preset key from [`RUNTIME_PRESETS`], or the
alias of an existing `runtime-profiles.<alias>`.

pricing.description:
Optional pricing data keyed by model id. Populated when the
provider's `/models` endpoint returns pricing (Kilo Gateway,
OpenRouter, etc.). Absent for catalog fallbacks without pricing.

CertRenewParams.description:
Params for `cert/renew`, served only on the mutually authenticated WSS
plane. The certificate renewed is the calling connection's own.

csr_pem.description: PEM-encoded certificate signing request for the replacement.

ChannelAlias.description: One configured channel instance an SOP channel trigger can bind to.

ChannelQuickStart.description: One channel selection submitted by the Quickstart builder.

alias.description:
User-named alias for this channel entry. Defaults to
`channel_type` in the UI; users override when stacking
multiple aliases of the same channel type.

channel_type.description:
Channel type identifier (`cli`, `telegram`, `discord`, `web`
in the FTUE-supported set).

fields.description:
Round-trip of every field the daemon described in
`quickstart/fields`. Surfaces echo back exactly what was
emitted; the daemon writes each entry under `<prefix>.<key>`
using its own schema knowledge.

ChannelTriggerKind.description:
One channel type row: every inbound-capable `ChannelKind` appears,
configured or not, so editors can offer setup for missing ones.

condition.description:
Condition payload contract for a channel-message trigger. Channel
payloads are arbitrary, so this is the `open` contract; carried per row
so the builder reads one shape whether the source is bound or a channel.

CommandDescriptor.description: Command identity and accepted tokens advertised to an RPC client.

ConditionField.description:
One field of a trigger payload a condition can reference. `path` is the
JSON path suffix after `$.` (empty for a scalar payload compared directly),
`label` is the human name, `value_type` drives the value control, and
`options` carries the choices when `value_type` is `Enum`.

ConditionOpSpec.description:
Wire shape of one operator for authoring surfaces: the literal `token` to
splice into a condition string, and a human `label` to show in a picker.

ConditionValueType.description:
Value-input widget hint for one condition field, so the authoring surface
renders the right control (text box, number, checkbox, enum select) and
quotes string comparands correctly.

oneOf.description: One of a finite set carried in `ConditionField::options`.
ISO-8601 instant; rendered as a datetime control, compared as a string.

ConfigSectionEntry.description: A config section entry for the dashboard sidebar / TUI section list.

group.description: Display group for the dashboard sidebar.

is_quickstart.description: `true` when this section is part of the canonical Quickstart list.

ready.description:
Whether the section currently has enough usable config for the
first-run path.

shape.description:
Editor shape (direct form / one-tier alias map / typed-family map /
backend picker).

ConfigSetManyParams.description:
An ordered batch of `config/set` entries committed as one unit: every
entry is staged on a single working copy in order (a later entry for
the same prop wins), and the result is saved and installed once, or
not at all. Must contain at least one entry and at most the
dispatcher's batch cap (256); either bound violated is `INVALID_PARAMS`.

props.description: The props written, in request order.

ConfigSetParams.description:
Value is polymorphic: a JSON string passes through as-is (backward
compat); any other JSON type is coerced via `coerce_for_set_prop`.

ConfigStatusResult.description: Config readiness status for the dashboard/TUI.

ConfigTemplateEntry.description:
Owned wire representation of a [`zeroclaw_config::traits::MapKeySection`].
The upstream type uses `&'static str` fields that can't round-trip
through `Deserialize`, so this owned copy serves as the wire format.

by_agent.description:
Breakdown by agent alias. Empty when `[cost].track_per_agent =
false` or when no records carry an agent_alias.

agent_alias.description:
Agent alias this job runs under. Empty when the row was written
before the column existed and no agent has claimed it; the
scheduler skips such rows with a warning rather than coercing
them to a magic alias.

shell_output_format.description:
Output format for shell jobs. `"wrapped"` (default) or `"raw"`.
Declarative jobs read this from `CronJobDecl.shell_output_format` in
the config; imperative jobs read it from the stored field in the DB.

source.description: How the job was created: `"imperative"` (CLI/API) or `"declarative"` (config).

uses_memory.description:
Whether to recall and inject memory context before this agent job runs.
Defaults to `true`; set to `false` for stateless digest jobs that should
not accumulate or consume memory entries.

delivery.description:
Delivery axis (`not_required | delivered | failed | skipped`).
`None` on rows recorded before the triple existed.

executing_agent.description:
The executing agent's canonical alias at time of action. `None` on
rows recorded before provenance existed.

execution.description:
Execution axis of the separated run-outcome triple (`ok | error`).
`None` on rows recorded before the triple existed.

job_source.description:
The job's `source` (`imperative` / `declarative`) at time of action;
keeps a run row retained past its job's deletion reachable by the
cleanup that owns that id space. `None` on rows recorded before
provenance existed.

owner_agent.description:
Durable CURRENT cleanup owner: stamped as the executing agent at
insert and re-pointed by agent renames, unlike the immutable
`executing_agent` historical fact. Owner-scoped deletion and
authorized retained-row reads key on this. How a `None` (pre-column
row) resolves — live-job fallback or quarantine — is owned by the
store's read/upgrade paths; see `list_runs_for_agent` and
`initialize_schema` in `cron::store`.

persistence.description:
Persistence axis (`not_bound | persisted | failed`). `None` on rows
recorded before the triple existed.

principal.description:
The initiating principal stamped at dispatch, verbatim — immune to
later job renames or owner changes. `None` on rows recorded before
provenance existed.

CronSettingsParams.description:
Params for `cron/settings`. Without a `patch` key, or with no params
at all, the call reads the scheduler settings. The daemon treats any
`patch` key as a write request, which it does not implement yet.

patch.description:
A present `null` stays `Some(Value::Null)`: the key's presence,
not its value, is what asks for a write.

CronShellOutputFormat.description: Output format for shell cron job stdout.

oneOf.description:
Wrapped format: `status=...
stdout:
...
stderr:
...` (default).

Raw stdout on a zero process exit; wrapped status/stdout/stderr on a
non-zero exit; a plain error string for failures that never reach a
process exit (security denial, spawn/setup failure, timeout).

DiagResult.description: Structured diagnostic result for programmatic consumption (web dashboard, API).

log_path.description: Resolved active log persistence path, if available.

FetchedCatalog.description:
One fetched catalogue's bytes, returned over the wire so the client writes
them into its own config dir (keeping the write in the caller's permission
scope).

default.description:
Pre-filled default the modal should show as ghost text /
initial input value. `None` when the schema has no meaningful
default for this field (e.g. API keys, bot tokens).

enum_variants.description: Closed-set choices for `Enum` kind. `None` for everything else.

help.description: One-line help blurb. Empty when the schema field has no doc.

is_secret.description: `true` for `#[secret]` fields — the modal masks input.

key.description:
Schema-side field key (kebab-case terminal segment). The
caller submits this back through [`BuilderSubmission`].

kind.description:
Wire-tag for the input control to render. Mirrors
`PropKind::wire_name`.

label.description: Human label shown next to the input.

required.description:
`true` when Quickstart treats this field as required. Currently
every field returned by [`field_shape`] is required, but the
flag is exposed so future additions can include optional rows.

FieldSection.description:
Selector kinds that the Quickstart "field shape" descriptor
covers. The TUI / web ask the runtime for the shape, then render
inputs dumbly off the response.

FileEntry.description:
A single file entry in a `file/attach` request. Either `path` (daemon
reads from local disk — Unix socket only) or `data_b64` (client sends
base64-encoded bytes) must be present.

mime_type.description:
Advisory only, retained for wire compatibility. The image/document
marker decision is made from the filename and payload bytes via the
canonical provider-loadable contract, never from this field.

FileEntryResult.description: Result for a single file in a `file/attach` response.

FileSource.description: Source hint for how the client obtained the file.

FileUploadBeginParams.description: Parameters for `file/upload/begin`: announce one upload for a session.

filename.description: Display name, at most 255 bytes; storage is content-addressed.

sha256.description: Optional hex SHA-256 of the whole payload, verified at commit.

size_bytes.description: Exact decoded size of the whole payload.

max_bytes.description: Largest payload an upload may declare.

upload_id.description: Identifies the upload on this connection only.

FileUploadChunkParams.description:
Parameters for `file/upload/chunk`. Chunks arrive in order: `offset`
must equal the bytes received so far. Resending an already-accepted
chunk with identical bytes is acknowledged without change.

FileUploadCommitParams.description:
Parameters for `file/upload/commit`. The result is the same
`FileEntryResult` that `file/attach` returns for one file.

FilesystemEventKind.description: A normalized filesystem change kind reported by the watcher.

FlowRole.description:
Why a flow wire exists. Mirrors the `StepRouting`/`StepFailure` field it
was derived from, so an editor can write edits back to the right place.

oneOf.description: Implicit fallthrough or explicit `routing.next`.
`routing.depends_on` fan-in: source must complete before target runs.
`on_failure: goto` recovery edge.
Named conditional port from `routing.switch`.
Derived from the SOP's triggers; read-only, never hand-wired.

FsEntry.description: A single directory entry returned by `fs.list_dir`.

path.description: Relative or absolute path within the agent workspace.

GateOnError.description: What the gate does when the model cannot answer (network, HTTP, malformed).

oneOf.description: Start the run anyway, in the strictest listed mode, so a human sees it.
Do not start the run. The event is recorded as skipped.

GraphDiagnostic.description:
A validation finding anchored to a step. Errors block saving
(`validate_sop_strict`); warnings render but do not block.

GraphLayout.description:
Deterministic auto-layout so every surface renders the same picture
without a client-side layout engine.

GraphNode.description:
A node in the projected graph: one SOP step, or one synthetic trigger
entry (`step >= TRIGGER_NODE_BASE`, `trigger_index` set).

GraphPin.description:
One connection point on a node. Flow pins order execution; data pins
carry the step's declared input/output schema type.

GraphWire.description:
A directed edge between two nodes. `flow_role` is set for flow wires;
data wires carry the producer/consumer pin names instead.

auth_provider.description:
Which configured provider verifies `auth_token` (e.g. `native`,
`oidc.corp`). Defaults to `native`. Selection is explicit and
final: the selected provider's denial never falls through to
another provider.

auth_token.description:
Explicit credential for authentication (a native pairing token
or an OIDC access token). Wins over the transport-intrinsic
peer credential when present.

env.description:
Shell environment from the TUI process, used to forward the user's
real env (PATH, credentials, etc.) to subprocesses spawned by the
daemon on their behalf. Omitted by older clients; defaults to empty.

tui_id.description: TUI ID from a previous connection (reconnection).

tui_sig.description: HMAC signature proving ownership of the claimed TUI ID.

commands.description:
Shared command catalogue entries available on the TUI surface.

Always serialized so a new daemon's authoritative empty catalogue
remains distinguishable from an older daemon that predates this
field.

principal_id.description: Canonical principal id this connection is bound to.

server_pid.description: OS process ID of the daemon serving this connection.

tui_sig.description: HMAC signature for reconnection. Pass back in next initialize.

InteractionSurface.description:
Closed identifier supplied by a trusted interaction client. The identifier
selects host-owned descriptive semantics; it never carries prompt prose or
capability claims from the client.

InternalPrincipal.description:
The runtime-owned principal that initiated an internally driven turn —
who caused the turn to exist, distinct from the executing agent identity
the turn runs under. Stamped once at dispatch from the runtime's own
resolved state (job config, canonical agent alias, runtime task id),
never from message content or tool arguments, and immutable for the
turn's lifetime. Persisted records carry it verbatim as at-time-of-action
fact. Internal principals never appear in `peer_groups` and are never
consulted by peer-membership checks — identity and delivery permission
are separate axes.

oneOf.description:
A scheduled cron job. `job_id` is the stable store id; `job_name`
the operator-facing name, if the job has one.

A peer-agent dispatch. `sender_alias` is the sending agent's
canonical alias — the initiator only; the recipient turn executes
under the recipient's own alias.

A daemon-driven task (heartbeat pipeline, SOP step driver). `task`
is a runtime-owned identifier, never model-authored text.

LayoutGeometry.description:
Canvas geometry carried on every serialized graph so the web canvas reads
placement pitch from the wire instead of a local literal. The values are
fixed by [`LayoutGeometry::CANONICAL`]; the struct rides on `GraphLayout`
only to expose them to non-Rust surfaces.

LocaleOption.description: One selectable locale from the build's embedded `locales.toml` registry.

LocalesFetchRequest.description:
Request payload for `locales/fetch`. `catalog` restricts which catalogues
are downloaded; `None`/empty means all. The daemon validates `locale`
against the embedded registry and `catalog` against the fixed catalog set.

skipped.description: Catalogue names that had no file on upstream and were skipped.

LocalesListResponse.description: Response for `locales/list` — the in-memory locale registry.

LogsGetParams.description: `logs/get` params — fetch a single event by id.

LogsGetResult.description:
`logs/get` result. `event` is the full `LogEvent` payload
(attributes, attribution map, span ids, …) that the Logs pane
only renders inside the detail modal — list rows store
preview-only data.

sop_run_id.description:
Exact SOP run correlation. Uses the canonical persisted-log
attribution filter, including its compatibility bridge for older rows.

until_line_offset.description:
Byte offset to resume reading from. Set from the previous
`LogsQueryResult::next_cursor_line_offset` for deterministic
pagination regardless of id ordering.

until_segment_cursor.description:
Segment-aware cursor. Set from `LogsQueryResult::next_segment_cursor`
to paginate across rotated archive files. Takes precedence over
`until_line_offset` when both are supplied.

incomplete.description:
True when a retained segment could not be read and was left out of
this page. `at_end` then means "no older events among the segments
that could be read", which is weaker than "no older events exist",
so a client that stops paging on `at_end` should say the history is
partial rather than present it as complete.

log_path.description: Resolved path of the active installed persistence writer.

next_cursor.description:
Legacy cursor. Deprecated since 0.8.0; tracked for removal in
<https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8012>.

next_cursor_line_offset.description:
Byte offset past the last event on this page. Callers should
pass this back as `until_line_offset` on the next request to
resume without re-scanning already-read bytes.

For multi-segment deployments, this is `None` when the oldest event
on the page is in an archive file — use `next_segment_cursor` instead.

next_segment_cursor.description:
Segment-aware cursor for the oldest event on this page. Pass back
as `until_segment_cursor` to walk older pages across segment
boundaries. Supersedes `next_cursor_line_offset` for `rotating`-mode
deployments with multiple retained segments.

LogsSubscribeResult.description:
Every notification of the subscription carries `subscription_id` and
its `seq`. `seq` here is the newest sequence number at subscribe time.

epoch.description: The hub's epoch: pass it back with `since_seq` to resume.

MapKeyKind.description:
Stable wire-form for an addable section — a `HashMap<String, T>` (Map) or
`Vec<T>` (List) field whose value type implements `Configurable`. The
dashboard / CLI use this to surface `+ Add` affordances without
hardcoding the section list. Auto-discovered by the `Configurable` derive.

oneOf.description: `HashMap<String, T>` — key is user-supplied; new value is default.

`Vec<T>` — entries are appended; the user-supplied "key" is stored
in the value type's natural identifier field (e.g. `name`, `hint`).

MemoryBackendKind.description: Selects the memory backend used by an agent.

oneOf.description: No memory backend. Recall returns empty; stores are no-ops.

Embedded SQLite (`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/sqlite.rs`). Default for
new installs because every supported platform can run it without
extra services.

PostgreSQL with optional pgvector
(`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/postgres.rs`, feature `memory-postgres`).
Qdrant vector store (`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/qdrant.rs`).

Markdown files in the agent's workspace
(`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/markdown.rs`).

Hybrid local SQLite + external Lucid CLI
(`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/lucid.rs`).

MemoryGetParams.description: `memory/get` params — fetch one entry's full content by key.

MemoryGetResult.description:
`memory/get` result. `entry` carries the full content
the Memory pane only renders inside the detail modal —
list rows store preview-only data.

plane.description:
Memory plane: `"private"` (the caller's own; the default for every
authenticated principal) or `"shared"` (honoured only for callers
with the admin bypass, audited).

completion.description: Output/completion tokens per-token rate (USD per token, e.g. `"0.000020"` = $20/1M tokens).

input_cache_read.description:
Cached input read rate — per-token charge for reading cached prompt data
(USD per token, e.g. `"0.000001"` = $1/1M tokens). Kilo Gateway specific.

input_cache_write.description:
Cached input write rate — per-token charge for writing prompt data to cache
(USD per token, e.g. `"0.000001"` = $1/1M tokens). Kilo Gateway specific.

prompt.description: Input/prompt tokens per-token rate (USD per token, e.g. `"0.000005"` = $5/1M tokens).

ModelProviderChoice.description: Model provider selection submitted by the Quickstart builder.

alias.description:
User-named alias. Defaults to `"default"` in the UI; users
override when stacking multiple aliases of the same provider
type (e.g. `anthropic-work`, `anthropic-personal`).

fields.description:
Round-trip of every field the daemon described in
`quickstart/fields`. Surfaces echo back exactly what was
emitted; the daemon writes each entry under `<prefix>.<key>`
using its own schema knowledge.

model.description:
Model id written to `providers.models.<type>.<alias>.model` at
apply time.

provider_type.description:
Provider type identifier (`anthropic`, `openai`, `openrouter`,
`ollama`, etc.). Used as the type segment in the TOML path.

cached_input_tokens.description: Total cached input tokens for this model

input_tokens.description: Total input tokens for this model

model.description: Model name (upstream resource id from usage telemetry).

output_tokens.description: Total output tokens for this model

request_count.description: Number of LLM responses for this model.

unpriced_tokens.description:
Tokens from records that explicitly report unavailable pricing.

Legacy ledger rows omit `pricing_available` and deserialize as priced,
so they do not contribute to this total.

oneOf.description: An executable SOP step.
A synthetic entry node representing one of the SOP's triggers.

NodePosition.description:
Grid placement for one node: column = longest flow path from an entry,
row = order of insertion within that column. `x`/`y` carry a persisted
canvas coordinate when the node has been dragged; absent otherwise.

NodeRunOverlay.description:
Run state for one step node. Trigger nodes carry no run state and are
omitted from overlays.

tool_calls.description:
Tool invocations captured while the step executed. Empty for
unreached steps and runs recorded before capture landed.

NodeRunState.description: Per-node execution state projected from a run's step results.

oneOf.description: Not reached yet (or run ended before reaching it).
The run's current step while the run is live.

OptionDomain.description:
Closed set of runtime-resolvable option domains a tool parameter can
draw its values from. Tools *declare* the domain; resolution happens
where live config is visible (the runtime), so surfaces render real
selectable choices instead of free-text guessing.

oneOf.description: Configured channel refs the agent listens on (e.g. `telegram.prod`).

Peers reachable by this agent: peer agents, external peers, and
peer groups. Cascades on a sibling `channel` argument when present.
Configured peer group names.
Configured agent aliases.
Names of tools registered in the active tool set.
Memory categories present in the configured backend.

PayloadContract.description:
The set of payload fields a condition may reference for a given source.
`open` marks sources whose payload is arbitrary user JSON (MQTT, AMQP,
webhook body, channel message): the surface offers a guided path/op/value
builder plus a sample-payload probe rather than a fixed field list. `direct`
marks a scalar payload (peripheral signal) compared with the bare `op value`
form and no path.

oneOf.description: Execution-order edge: which step runs after which.
Typed data edge derived from a `{{steps.N}}` binding.

PlanEntry.description:
A single plan entry. ACP-shaped (`content`/`priority`/`status`) plus
the optional ZeroClaw `active_form` extension.

PlanPriority.description:
Relative importance of a plan entry. Defaults to `Medium` when a
caller omits it; ACP requires `priority` on the outward projection,
so normalization to a concrete value happens at parse time here.

PlanStatus.description:
Execution status of a single plan entry. Snake-case on the wire to
match ACP (`in_progress`).

PlannedToolCall.description:
An authored tool invocation planned for a step. Args may embed
`{{steps.N.path}}` / `{{calls.K.path}}` bindings (see `sop::binding`)
that resolve against captured run data before dispatch. `pinned`
carries a sample output (typically lifted from a real run's
`StepToolCall.output_data`) so downstream bindings can be authored
and previewed without re-executing the tool.

args.description: Argument template; string leaves may contain bindings.

PropKind.description: Runtime type classification for config property values.

oneOf.description: An enum or other serde-serializable type (parsed as TOML string).
A reference to a configured alias; `alias_source` names the namespace.
A `Vec<String>` field; set via comma-separated input.

QuickstartApplyResult.description: Tagged enum — matches the HTTP route's `ApplyResult` shape.

daemon_restarted.description:
`true` when the in-place daemon reload was signalled.
`false` when no reload tx was attached (e.g. test harness)
— caller must restart the daemon manually to pick up the
change.

surface.description:
Surface that emitted the dismissal. Deserialised straight
into the typed enum — no string-match at the boundary.

QuickstartPeerGroup.description:
Peer-group entry staged in the Quickstart. Maps 1:1 to a
`[peer_groups.<name>]` table written at apply time. The `channel`
field carries a `<type>.<alias>` ref pointing at either a staged
channel from the same submission or a pre-existing one.

channel.description: Channel ref (`<type>.<alias>`) the peer group authorizes.

external_peers.description: External (non-agent) peer usernames the channel should accept.

ignore.description: Per-group blocklist applied to the resolved peer set.

name.description:
Map key written to `peer_groups.<name>`. Synthesized by surfaces
from the channel ref so no `match` table is involved.

QuickstartPersonalityFile.description:
One personality file staged for write during Quickstart apply.
The runtime writes `<workspace>/<filename>` with `content`,
overwriting if the path already exists.

content.description: File body. Subject to `MAX_FILE_CHARS` at apply time.

channel_types.description:
Picker rows for "Create new channel" — sourced from the
schema's `ChannelsConfig` by walking its serialised
top-level keys, so adding a channel family in the schema
surfaces here automatically.

default_runtime_profile.description: Canonical runtime fallback for providers without a recommendation.

model_provider_types.description:
Picker rows for "Create new model provider" — sourced from
the canonical `zeroclaw_providers::list_model_providers()`
registry by the runtime's `quickstart::snapshot_state`.

unassigned_channels.description:
Subset of `channels` not yet bound to any agent — safe to
reuse without breaking the one-channel-one-agent invariant.

QuickstartTypeOption.description:
One row in the Quickstart "Create new …" picker. The TUI and
web surfaces both render this list as-is — no hardcoded
option lists on either side.

default_runtime_profile.description: Daemon-derived runtime preset to auto-select for this provider.

kind.description:
Canonical kebab-case identifier written into config
(`anthropic`, `telegram`, `wecom-ws`, …).

local.description:
`true` when the entry runs locally and needs no remote
credential. Always `false` for channels.

QuickstartValidateResult.description:
Tagged enum — matches the HTTP route's `ValidateResult` shape so
the drift test can compare bytes.

RunOverlay.description:
Live run state layered over a `SopGraph`, letting a canvas animate an
execution without re-fetching the graph. Served by `sops/run-overlay`.

SchedulerConfig.description:
Scheduler configuration for periodic task execution (`[scheduler]` section).

Owns the cron-runtime knobs: per-job declarations live on
`Config.cron: HashMap<String, CronJobDecl>` (alias-keyed), while the
scheduler loop's runtime behavior (`enabled`, polling cap, catch-up) lives here.

catch_up_on_startup.description:
Run all overdue jobs at scheduler startup. Default: `true`.

When the daemon restarts late, jobs whose `next_run` is in the past
fire once before normal polling resumes. Disable to wait for the
next scheduled occurrence instead.

enabled.description: Enable the built-in scheduler loop. When false, no cron jobs run.

max_concurrent.description: Maximum tasks executed in parallel within a single polling cycle.

max_run_history.description: Maximum number of historical cron run records to retain. Default: `50`.

max_tasks.description: Maximum number of persisted scheduled tasks per polling cycle.

SectionShape.description:
UI rendering shape for a section. Drives picker / form dispatch on
the `/config` curated section explorer and the Quickstart flow.

oneOf.description: `<section>` renders a schema-driven form with no picker step.

`<section>.<alias>` map of structured entries; the section page
shows an alias list with `+ Add` and clicking an alias opens its
schema form.

`<section>.<type>.<alias>` two-tier map. Picker chooses `<type>`,
alias-list step chooses `<alias>`, then the schema form opens.

Single non-alias choice (memory backend, tunnel provider). Picker
flips a top-level field, then the schema form for the chosen
backend/provider renders.

SelectorChoice.description: Selects either an existing configured value or a fresh builder value.

oneOf.description:
Use an already-configured alias under the corresponding
section. Carries only the alias key — the runtime resolves
against the live config at apply time.
Create a new entry from the carried value.

SelectorChoice2.description: Selects either an existing configured value or a fresh builder value.

oneOf.description:
Use an already-configured alias under the corresponding
section. Carries only the alias key — the runtime resolves
against the live config at apply time.
Create a new entry from the carried value.

SelectorChoice3.description: Selects either an existing configured value or a fresh builder value.

oneOf.description:
Use an already-configured alias under the corresponding
section. Carries only the alias key — the runtime resolves
against the live config at apply time.
Create a new entry from the carried value.

SelectorChoice4.description: Selects either an existing configured value or a fresh builder value.

oneOf.description:
Use an already-configured alias under the corresponding
section. Carries only the alias key — the runtime resolves
against the live config at apply time.
Create a new entry from the carried value.

SessionIdParams.description:
Shared param for methods that only need a session ID:
`session/close`, `session/cancel`, `session/messages`,
`session/state`, `session/delete`.

query.description:
Full-text search query. When present, only sessions whose message
content matches (via FTS5) are returned.

cursor.description:
Presence of this field opts into bounded ACP cursor pagination.
`null` requests the newest page; a string continues a walk.

start.description:
Index of the first entry in `messages` relative to the
full projected history. Pair with `total` to compute
"page N of M" / "load older" affordances.

total.description:
Total projected entries for this session. Lets the TUI know how
many pages remain before it reaches the head.

interaction_surface.description:
Closed user-facing harness identifier. The daemon validates this
value and resolves all descriptive claims from host-owned state.

keep_siblings.description:
When true, skip the same-mode idle-sibling eviction normally
performed on `session/new` for the calling TUI. Sent by
multi-session-aware clients that manage sibling session lifecycle
themselves. Absent or false preserves the eviction sweep.

tui_id.description:
Accepted for wire compatibility and ignored. The session's shell
environment is resolved from the calling connection's own TUI
registration, so naming another connection's id here has no
effect.

SessionOverrides.description: Per-session model and sampling overrides carried by `session/configure`.

attachments.description:
Inline file attachments. Processed identically to `file/attach`
entries — markers are appended to the prompt before the turn runs.

client_turn_generation.description:
Optional client-local turn identity echoed by `TurnComplete`.
Older clients omit this field and retain session-scoped behavior.

plan.description:
Authoritative live-session TodoWrite plan. Older/persisted
sessions omit this field because they have no runtime plan owner.

SessionUpdateEvent.description:
Typed session update events pushed via `session/update` notifications.
Replaces the hand-built `notification_for_turn_event` function.

oneOf.description:
Per-LLM-call token usage. `input_tokens` is the cumulative context size
for this turn. `max_context_tokens` is the preemptive-trim budget (the
resolved `effective_context_budget`), preserving its original meaning as
the value the meter fills toward. `model_context_window` is the model's
full context window (provider `context_window`), exposed distinctly so a
client can render capacity and budget separately. Any may be absent when
the provider doesn't report usage or the value can't be resolved.

Emitted when the TodoWrite tool produces a plan. The `entries` array
carries the normalized `PlanEntry` values (content, status, priority,
optional activeForm) so the client can render the live tracker.

Terminal event for a turn. Replaces the response of `session/prompt`.
`outcome` distinguishes a clean finish from a user-initiated cancel.

client_turn_generation.description:
Optional client-local turn identity, echoed from `session/prompt`.
Absent for legacy callers that do not send one.

content.description:
Final assistant text (Completed) or partial accumulated text
at cancel point (Cancelled).

message_count.description:
Authoritative projected conversation-entry count after this turn.
Absent for legacy or missing-session terminal events.

oneOf.description:
Emitted whenever older whole turns were dropped from structured history
to fit a token budget or message cap. Surfaces a user-visible "context
was cut here" marker so trimming is never silent. `dropped_messages` is
the count of conversation messages removed; `dropped_turns` and
`kept_turns` describe the user-facing whole-turn accounting.

token_budget.description:
Configured context token budget in effect at trim time. `None` for
message-limit trims, which carry no token accounting.

unsatisfiable_floor.description:
The retained provider-facing request cannot be brought under the
configured budget (protected newest turn plus schemas). History MAY
have been trimmed on the way to that floor, so this flag — not
`dropped_messages == 0` — is the authoritative "unsatisfiable"
signal. Absent for ordinary trims.

SkillBundleEntry.description: Wire representation of a skill bundle. Consolidates gateway `BundleEntry`.

always.description:
When `true`, keeps this skill's instructions inlined in the system
prompt even in compact skill-prompt mode. See `Skill::always`.

SkillListEntry.description: Wire representation of a skill in a list. Consolidates gateway `SkillEntry`.

SkillSlashChoice.description: A predefined choice for a typed slash option.

SkillSlashOption.description:
A typed option a `slash`-tagged skill exposes on its slash command. Shaped
after the Discord Application Command Option model but channel-agnostic; a
slash-capable channel maps `kind` to its wire option type. Declared in
SKILL.toml under `[[skill.slash_options]]`.

choices.description:
Predefined choices (string/integer/number options only). The `value` is
kept as text and coerced to the option's type by the channel.

description_localizations.description:
Per-locale translations of `description`, keyed by Discord locale code.
Empty for unlocalized options. Declared under
`[[skill.slash_options]]` as `description_localizations`.

type.description:
`string` | `integer` | `number` | `boolean` | `user` | `channel` |
`role` | `mentionable`. Unknown values are dropped by the channel.

Sop.description: A complete Standard Operating Procedure definition.

admission_policy.description:
How to handle a trigger that cannot be admitted immediately because this
SOP's execution slots are full (A2). Default `parallel`.

agent.description:
Parent agent alias that owns this procedure. Every `execute` step runs
as this agent unless the step names its own `agent` override. Required
for headless triggers (mqtt, webhook, cron, amqp), which have no
ambient agent loop to borrow.

cooldown_secs.description:
Minimum seconds between successive runs of this procedure. `0`
(default) disables the cooldown and back-to-back runs are allowed.

decision.description:
Optional decision-model gate and execution-mode choice, from the
`[decision]` table of `SOP.toml`. See [`super::decision`].

description.description:
Free-text summary of what the procedure does and when it fires. Shown
in the SOP list and header; purely descriptive, never executed.

deterministic.description:
When true, sets execution_mode to Deterministic.
Steps execute sequentially without LLM round-trips.

execution_mode.description:
How steps are driven: `auto`, `supervised` (default), `step_by_step`,
`priority_based`, or `deterministic`. `deterministic = true` forces
the last regardless of this field.

max_concurrent.description:
Maximum simultaneous runs of this one procedure. Excess trigger
firings queue or drop per the engine's concurrency policy. Default 1.

max_pending_approvals.description:
Upper bound on runs of this SOP parked at a HITL approval at once
(`0` = unlimited). Once reached, further triggers are deferred (surfaced for
backpressure/redelivery) rather than silently dropped. Default `0`.

name.description:
Unique procedure name. Doubles as the on-disk directory key, so a
rename in the editor moves the SOP's folder. Must be non-empty.

priority.description:
Scheduling priority when concurrency limits force a choice between
runnable procedures: `critical`, `high`, `normal` (default), `low`.

steps.description:
Ordered step definitions. This is the body of the procedure; the
daemon renumbers and remaps routing refs on save.

triggers.description:
Signals that start a run. A procedure may bind several triggers; any
one firing (subject to its own condition) launches the SOP.

version.description:
Semantic version string for the procedure definition (e.g. `1.0.0`).
Bump it when you change step behavior so runs are traceable.

SopAdmissionPolicy.description:
How concurrent triggers are handled when a SOP's execution slots are full. A
run parked at a HITL approval releases its slot (A1), so this governs the
remaining case: too many runs actively *executing* at once. No variant ever
silently drops a trigger except `Drop`, which is explicit opt-in.

oneOf.description:
Admit up to `max_concurrent` concurrent runs; a trigger that cannot admit
now is DEFERRED (surfaced for backpressure/redelivery), never silently
dropped. Best fit for independent work like PR-request approvals.

Serialize: admit only when no run of this SOP is active or parked; other
triggers are deferred. For pipelines whose pre-approval steps must not overlap.

Collapse concurrent triggers: when a run is already in flight for this SOP a
new trigger is coalesced (dropped as redundant - the in-flight run already
covers the latest state). For "only current state matters" SOPs.

Legacy fire-and-forget: a trigger that cannot admit now is dropped. Explicit
opt-in only; never the default.

SopDecideRequest.description:
Request payload for `sops/decide`: resolve a paused checkpoint. `name` and
`run_id` select the run; `decision` is the raw `ApprovalDecision` wire value
(`"approve"` or `{"deny": {"reason": "..."}}`), deserialized into the
canonical runtime enum by the handler so no parallel decision enum exists
here to drift from it.

gate.description:
Yes/no question asked about each matching event. The run starts only
when the model's "yes" probability reaches `gate_threshold`.

gate_on_error.description:
When the model cannot answer: `run_strict` starts the run under the
fail-closed mode, `skip` does not start it.

gate_threshold.description: Minimum "yes" probability (0 to 1) for the gate to start a run.

min_confidence.description: A mode choice below this confidence falls back to the strictest mode.

mode_instructions.description: Guidance for the mode choice (what makes a run routine vs. risky).

model.description: Alias of the decision model to ask, from `[decision_models.<alias>]`.

modes.description:
Execution modes the model may choose between for this run. Empty keeps
the SOP's authored `execution_mode`. Only `auto`, `supervised`, and
`step_by_step` are selectable.

part_threshold.description:
Minimum "yes" probability for a step's `decide` question to include
that step (a conditional part).

SopDraftParams.description:
Params for `sops/graph-draft`: project an unsaved SOP (the `sops/save`
wire form) onto its graph without persisting it.

SopExecutionMode.description: How much autonomy the agent has when executing an SOP.

oneOf.description: Execute all steps without human approval.
Request approval before starting, then execute all steps.
Request approval before each step.
Critical/High → Auto, Normal/Low → Supervised.

Execute steps sequentially without LLM round-trips.
Step outputs are piped as inputs to the next step.
Checkpoint steps pause for human approval.

SopGraph.description:
The full projected graph: nodes, wires, validation diagnostics, and a
precomputed layout. Serialized as-is over RPC (`sops/graph`) and HTTP.

SopPriority.description: SOP priority level, used for execution mode resolution and scheduling.

SopRenameRequest.description:
Request payload for `sops/rename`: move the SOP stored under `from` to
`to`. Rename is its own operation rather than a side effect of `sops/save`
because saving persists under the submitted SOP's name, so a name change
smuggled through a save would fork the SOP or overwrite a different one.

from.description: Name the SOP is stored under today.

to.description: Name to move it to. Must not already be taken.

SopRunOverlayRequest.description:
Request payload for `sops/run-overlay`: project a run's state onto a SOP's
graph. Selects the SOP by `name` and the run by `run_id`.

SopRunRequest.description:
Request payload for `sops/run`: fire a Manual trigger for the named SOP.
`payload` is an optional JSON string handed to the run as the step-1 input;
omitting it starts the run with no payload. The daemon builds the Manual
`SopEvent` and dispatches it on the same path as the `sop_execute` tool.

dedup_key.description:
Optional semantic work-item key shared with another trigger producer.
Dispatch coalesces matching keys only while the first run remains active.

SopRunResponse.description:
Response payload for `sops/run`: the id of the run that was started, which
feeds straight into `sops/run-overlay` to animate the run on the canvas.

SopRunStatus.description: Status of an SOP execution run.

oneOf.description:
An operator requested cancellation while work was in flight. The run
remains active and keeps its admission claim until the driver reaches
the next supported step boundary.
Paused at a checkpoint in a deterministic workflow.

SopRunsRequest.description:
Request payload for `sops/runs`: enumerate runs the engine currently holds
(active plus retained terminal), newest first. `sop` optionally scopes the
listing to a single SOP by name; omitting it lists every SOP's runs.

SopSaveRequest.description:
Request payload for `sops/save` and `sops/create`. The `sop` field is the
wire form of the runtime `Sop`; the daemon deserializes and validates it.
`sops/validate` also accepts this form to validate an unsaved draft.

SopSelectRequest.description:
Request payload for SOP read/delete methods that select one SOP by name:
`sops/get`, `sops/graph`, `sops/validate` (by name), `sops/delete`.

SopStep.description: A single step in an SOP procedure, parsed from SOP.md.

agent.description:
Agent alias that runs this step. Overrides the SOP's parent agent when
set; unset inherits the parent. Authored, persisted, and resolved into
the executing action via `effective_agent` (step override then parent).
Spawning a distinct per-step agent's own session at execution time is
staged follow-on work; today the resolved alias is stamped on the action
and the active agent loop executes the step body.

body.description:
The step's instruction body in Markdown. This is the prompt the
running agent executes for the step; bindings like `{{steps.N}}`
resolve against prior step outputs at run time.

calls.description:
Ordered tool calls planned for this step. Args may carry
`{{steps.N}}` / `{{calls.K}}` bindings validated at save time.

decide.description:
Conditional part (`- decide:` bullet): a yes/no question the SOP's
decision model answers about the triggering event when the run starts,
in the same call as the SOP's gate. The step runs only on "yes"
(p(yes) at or above `[decision] part_threshold`); on "no" it is recorded
as skipped and the run moves on. If the model cannot answer, it runs.

edit.description:
Editable-field opt-in for a checkpoint step (`- edit: body` bullet): the
named field of the piped value an approver may amend before the run
resumes (the gate prompt gains an "Edit" choice). Absent = no editing.

gate_prompt.description:
Authored gate-notice template for a HITL step (`- prompt:` bullet).
`{{path.to.field}}` placeholders resolve against the step's piped input
(the trigger payload at step 1, the previous step's output later) — pure
lookups, no logic. Rendered into the out-of-band approval notice so the
approver sees WHAT they are approving; absent = an automatic summary.

number.description:
Ordinal position of this step within the procedure. Steps run in
number order unless routing overrides the sequence; the daemon
renumbers on save so gaps and reorders normalize to 1..N.

on_failure.description: Failure handling metadata. Default preserves fail-the-run behavior.

policy.description:
Approval policy name (a key in `[sop.approval].policies`) the approval broker
enforces for this step's gate: required approver group + quorum. `None` keeps
today's behavior (`approval_mode` alone governs, no membership/quorum).

pos.description:
Persisted canvas coordinate, set by dragging the node in the Blueprint
editor. Absent until the node is moved; not surfaced in the step form.

requires_confirmation.description:
Pause for human confirmation before this step runs. Independent of
`checkpoint` kind and the SOP-level approval gate; both still apply.

routing.description: Conditional routing metadata. Default preserves linear execution.

schema.description: Typed input/output schemas for deterministic data flow validation.

scope.description: Tool scope for this step. `suggested_tools` remains the legacy alias.

title.description:
Short human label for the step, shown on the canvas node and in the
step list. Leave blank and the surface falls back to "untitled".

unless_decided.description:
Skip this step when step N's `decide` question was answered "yes"
(`- unless_decided: N` bullet). Lets one decision select between
alternative sets of steps, e.g. a scope hold instead of a full review.

with.description: Capability arguments, serialized as `with` in TOML/JSON definitions.

SopStepKind.description: The kind of a workflow step.

oneOf.description: Normal step — executed by the agent (or deterministic handler).
Checkpoint step — pauses execution and waits for human approval.
Deterministic capability step - executed by the SOP capability registry.

SopTrigger.description: What event can activate an SOP.

oneOf.description: MQTT message arrival. Live: delivered by the MQTT listener.

condition.description:
Optional expression evaluated against the message payload; the run
starts only when it holds.

topic.description: Topic filter. `+` matches one level, `#` matches the remaining levels.

oneOf.description: Inbound HTTP request. Live: gateway `/sop/*` and SOP-first `/webhook` routes.

path.description: Request path matched exactly against the event path.

oneOf.description: Time-based firing. Live: dispatched by the SOP maintenance tick (daemon / channel-start paths).

expression.description: Cron expression evaluated over the run window.

oneOf.description: Hardware signal. Defined and matched, but no peripheral listener feeds it.

board.description: Board identifier the signal originates from.

condition.description: Optional expression evaluated against the signal payload.

signal.description: Signal name on the board; matched as `board/signal`.

oneOf.description: Filesystem change. Live: delivered by the filesystem watcher.

condition.description: Optional expression evaluated against the change payload.

events.description: Change kinds to match; empty matches every kind.

path.description: Path glob (`*`, `**`, `?`); a bare directory matches anything under it.

oneOf.description: Calendar event state. Defined and matched, but no poller feeds it live.

calendar_ids.description: Calendar IDs to scope to; empty matches all of the source's calendars.

calendar_source.description: Calendar source identifier the event originates from.

condition.description: Optional expression evaluated against the calendar event payload.

oneOf.description:
Inbound message or forge/platform event on a configured channel
(telegram, discord, slack, git, ...). Live: delivered by the channel
orchestrator when the channel's SOP dispatch is enabled. The Git forge
producer sets an event topic of the form `<channel>.<alias>:<event_type>`
and puts `event_type` in the payload, so an authored `condition` filters
forge events by type without a second trigger shape.

alias.description: Optional configured-instance alias; unset matches every instance.

channel.description: `ChannelKind` snake_case value naming the channel type.

condition.description: Optional expression evaluated against the message payload.

oneOf.description: Agent-initiated run via the `sop_execute` tool. Not an external fan-in.
AMQP delivery. Live: delivered by the AMQP consumer in a SOP dispatch mode.

condition.description: Optional expression evaluated against the delivery body.

routing_key.description:
Routing-key filter (topic-exchange semantics): `.`-delimited words,
`*` matches one word, `#` matches zero or more words.

SopValidateParams.description:
Params for `sops/validate`: an unsaved draft in the `sops/save` form
(`sop`, optionally with `original_name`), or a stored SOP selected by
`name`. A request carrying a `sop` key is always validated as a draft,
and its `name` is then ignored.

SopWireDraftParams.description:
Params for `sops/wire-draft`: apply one wire edit to an unsaved SOP
(the `sops/save` wire form) and return the edited SOP and its graph.
The handler reads the two keys itself so each can report its own
error; this type is their declared contract.

StepFailure.description: Failure handling policy for a single SOP step.

StepPos.description:
Persisted canvas coordinate for a step node. Written by the Blueprint
editor when a node is dragged; never edited in the step-definition form.

StepRouting.description: Conditional routing metadata for a single SOP step.

depends_on.description: Step numbers that must have completed before this step can run.

switch.description:
Ordered switch ports. Non-empty makes this a multi-branch switch node:
each port is a named conditional out-edge, matched top to bottom.

terminal.description:
When true, this step ends its branch: no implicit fallthrough to the
following step is derived. Lets an authoring surface delete the default
sequence edge and leave a node free-floating between saves.

when.description: Guard evaluated against accumulated run data.

StepSchema.description:
JSON Schema fragment for validating step input/output data.
Stored as a raw `serde_json::Value` so callers can validate without
pulling in a full JSON Schema library.

input.description: JSON Schema object describing expected input shape.

output.description: JSON Schema object describing expected output shape.

StepToolCall.description:
One tool invocation captured during a step's execution. A step may
make any number of calls (including the same tool repeatedly);
`index` preserves invocation order so authoring surfaces can replay
the sequence and map data between calls.

index.description: Zero-based invocation order within the step.

output.description: Display text of the tool output.

output_data.description: Structured output when the tool declared one (`ToolOutput::data`).

StepToolScope.description: Per-step allow/deny tool scope. Enforcement is opt-in through SOP config.

allow.description: Only these names or groups are allowed when present.

deny.description: These names or groups are always subtracted.

epoch.description:
The `epoch` the client's `since_seq` came from (returned by the
subscribe result). Sequence numbers restart in every hub, so
`since_seq` resumes only when this matches the current epoch;
otherwise, or when omitted, every frame still buffered is replayed
after a `subscription/lagged` with `epoch_changed: true`.

since_seq.description:
Resume after this sequence number: frames from `since_seq + 1`
that are still buffered are replayed before live delivery. Omit
for live frames only.

cancelled.description:
`false` when no subscription with that id is open on this
connection (already ended, or never existed).

SubscriptionLagged.description:
`subscription/lagged`: frames `from_seq` up to (not including)
`resume_seq` are gone; delivery continues at `resume_seq`.

epoch_changed.description:
The client's `since_seq` came from another epoch (the daemon
restarted or reloaded). Nothing it saw can be matched here: this
epoch's frames from `resume_seq` on are replayed, and those before
it are gone.

Surface.description:
Which surface invoked the Quickstart. Stamped on every event in
the apply path so SSE/dashboard consumers can filter by origin
without parsing message strings.

SwitchRule.description:
A single named output port on a switch step. Rules are evaluated top to
bottom; the first whose `when` guard passes routes the run to `goto`. A
rule with `when` unset is the catch-all (n8n's "unknown"/default port) and
should be ordered last.

goto.description: Target step this port routes to.

name.description: Port label shown on the node's output pin (e.g. `pull_request`).

when.description: Guard evaluated against accumulated run data. `None` = catch-all.

TokenCountSource.description:
Provenance of a token count carried on a history-trim event. Lets clients
distinguish provider-reported usage from a local estimate and from a mix of
the two (the reported-budget trim path scales an estimate to a
provider-reported figure).

oneOf.description: Count comes from provider-reported usage.
Count is locally estimated.
Count is calibrated from provider-reported usage and a local estimate.

ToolsParamOptionsParams.description:
Params for `tools/param-options`: the option list for one tool
parameter domain.

agent.description:
Agent whose configuration scopes the options. Blank or absent
selects the first configured agent.

args.description: Domain-specific arguments, handed to the option resolver as-is.

TriggerField.description: One editable field of a trigger source (e.g. `topic` for MQTT).

TriggerFieldKind.description: Input widget hint for a trigger field.

oneOf.description: Free-form single value (topic, path, cron expression, ...).
Multi-value selection; `options` carries the choices when finite.
Condition expression evaluated against the trigger payload.

TriggerSourceRegistry.description:
Everything an authoring surface needs to offer trigger configuration:
the full ordered source list, the bound (non-channel) sources with their
field shapes, and per-channel availability. `Channel` is special-cased
into `channels` because its options depend on live config, not just the
enum; `sources` still names it so surfaces render the picker from one
backend-walked list instead of reconstructing it.

operators.description:
The comparison operators every condition builder renders. Read from
[`crate::sop::condition::ConditionOp`], never hand-listed by a surface.

connected_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp (for gateway API / web frontend).

connected_at_unix.description:
Unix epoch seconds (for TUI client relative-time display
without requiring chrono).

TurnCompletionOutcome.description:
Wire-stable subset of the runtime's `rpc::turn::TurnOutcome` for
`TurnComplete`. `messages` is intentionally not on the wire — the TUI
rebuilds from streamed chunks.

WireEdit.description:
One editor gesture. `role` picks which routing field is mutated; `port`
is required for `Switch` (index into `routing.switch`) and ignored
otherwise. Accepted over RPC (`sops/wire-draft`) and HTTP.

from.description: Source step number (the node the wire leaves).

port.description: Switch port index; grows the port list on connect if needed.

to.description: Target step number (the node the wire enters).

oneOf.description: Create the edge, overwriting any previous target of the same role.
Remove the edge only if it currently points at the given target.

info.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 methods served by `zeroclaw daemon` over the local socket or named pipe, framed as newline-delimited JSON. Generated by `cargo generate openrpc` from `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`; do not edit by hand. Framing, the handshake and transport rules are described in `rpc-socket.md`.
info.title: ZeroClaw daemon RPC

schema.description:
Which configured provider verifies `auth_token` (e.g. `native`,
`oidc.corp`). Defaults to `native`. Selection is explicit and
final: the selected provider's denial never falls through to
another provider.

Explicit credential for authentication (a native pairing token
or an OIDC access token). Wins over the transport-intrinsic
peer credential when present.

Shell environment from the TUI process, used to forward the user's
real env (PATH, credentials, etc.) to subprocesses spawned by the
daemon on their behalf. Omitted by older clients; defaults to empty.
TUI ID from a previous connection (reconnection).
HMAC signature proving ownership of the claimed TUI ID.
Free-form JSON shaped by the daemon at runtime.

Closed user-facing harness identifier. The daemon validates this
value and resolves all descriptive claims from host-owned state.

When true, skip the same-mode idle-sibling eviction normally
performed on `session/new` for the calling TUI. Sent by
multi-session-aware clients that manage sibling session lifecycle
